title: Triton callers pass frozen dimensions that their kernel bodies never read
executor_revision: external-bw1100-development-adapters; each campaign/development-binding.json owns its gateway revision

evidence.method: Parse every retained evaluation source with ast; compare annotated N_/D_ parameters against Name Load nodes in the kernel body. Select the retained starter/baseline per task. No generated source is imported or executed.
evidence.counterexample: aka_momentum_sgd reads all eight dimension parameters. Tiled candidates in other tasks also read bounds unused by their starters; parameter removal cannot depend on a name prefix or task label.

observation: All 29 starters on bw1100-1 and 23 of 24 on bw1100 contain unused kernel dimension parameters. Adadelta and AdamW each pass 14 dimension parameters with seven unused; aka_row_gather passes five with two unused. constants() emits every global dimension into the signature, per-call keywords and compile_constants. Existing device CSE, module-level launch binding and HCU pointer-range adapters are present in the frozen evidence and are not new findings. Callable latency does not identify how much time belongs to this redundancy.
proposed_change: Derive one live constant mapping from the complete emitted kernel body and use it for the kernel signature, host launch keywords and native compile_constants. Retain Schedule values for host grid construction and preserve num_warps, num_stages and register launch options independently. Preserve all dynamic ABI checks, fresh output allocation, caller-owned output validation, current pointer reads and Triton ownership of specialization, stream and launch. This changes lowering only; IR semantics, types, effects, verifier admission and arithmetic stay unchanged.
promotion_disposition: Prepared under issue #461 for independent review and software verification. The 81 changed Corpus sources have identical kernel-body ASTs; their complete Python ASTs differ only by removal of unused constexpr declarations and launch keywords. QSA v7 is a source-binding successor for four changed stages; v6, its original Compiler replay, Workload, composition and timing contracts are preserved. Device correctness and ordinary-call performance remain unmeasured for the successor, including NVIDIA QSA. No graph replay, output reuse or measurement-contract change is proposed. The original development Runs and diagnostic samples remain at their frozen Compiler.
